Historical July designs and subsequent retained studies.

# Question

Did the earlier joint-fitting designs and subsequent screens establish transferable parameters, or leave a bounded negative result?

# Result

The shared-ion density/speciation fit converged but worsened pressure. In its retained metric, pressure
training/active median absolute log error changed **0.432 → 0.869** and the
reserved comparison changed **0.542 → 0.730**.

# Basis and method

[]{#july-coupled-regression-designs}

The July designs specified a joint pressure/speciation objective, frozen
parameter bounds, grouped data partitions, multistart behavior and explicit
identification checks. The independent-assessment design separated fitting
rows from comparison rows and required coverage and failure accounting.

These documents recorded the estimation strategy and acceptance questions at
that stage. Later studies changed the active coordinates, model choices and
assessment sequence. The designs were never a parameter adoption and should
not be rerun simply because their prose is older.

# Values

[]{#what-was-learned-afterward}

| Study period | Retained outcome |
|:--|:--|
| 13 July | Joint pressure/speciation designs and independent-assessment design; no parameter adoption. |
| 28 July | Converged shared-ion fit; pressure errors worsened as reported above. |
| August | Pressure-first screening explored directions, conditioning, bounds and loading trends without resolving the coupled fit. The consolidated Issue 70 comparison did not establish transferable parameters. |
| Later reaction-temperature study | The later reaction-temperature study changed the question: equation-of-state (EOS) parameters were held fixed while two sensitivity directions spanning pressure, speciation and heat were tested. It improved pressure and heat more than speciation and left carbamate/bicarbonate partition unresolved. That is the retained lesson from the sequence. |

# Limits and evidence type

[]{#how-to-use-this-history}

Use the July records to avoid repeating objective-design work. A new numerical
study needs to state what changed in the question, inputs, model/Engine
identity or evidence. It must retain the exact data partition, evaluated and
failed states, residual definitions, parameter identity and independent
assessment rule. A historical design is retained background; it is not permission to
revive a discarded strategy or to promote its vector.

This is design history with retained calibration and comparison evidence, not independent physical validation.
